title: Control the Options: Get Others to Play with the Cards You Deal
coreMove: Design the available choices so the decision happens before the chooser notices the frame
sourcePressure: Chapter 31 centers on controlling the options so others appear free while choosing within a frame you designed. The law values menu control because outcomes are often decided before the final decision if the available paths already favor one result. Its limit is that option-shaping becomes coercive or brittle when the framing is too obvious, too narrow, or hides stakes others fairly need to understand. Frozen sidecar provides no traceable named anecdote for this chapter; do not fabricate named source anchors.
